la:adj:inhumanus.html:
ĭn-hūmānus, a, um, adj.,
not suitable to the human condition, that does not befit a human being.
Inhuman.
Rude, savage, barbarous: quis tam fuit durus et ferreus, quis tam inhumanus, qui non illorum miseria commoveretur,: vox,: scelus,: crudelitas,: via,covered with corpses,: securitas,that enjoyed itself during the slaughter,: testamentum,cruel, unjust,.—
Unpolished, uncivil, unmannerly, ill-bred, churlish, discourteous: quis contumacior, quis inhumanior, quis superbior,: moderati nec difficiles, nec inhumani senes,: at hoc idem si in convivio faciat, inhumanus videatur,ill-bred,: agrestis et inhumana neglegentia,: homo inhumanissimus,: aures,uncultivated,.—
Superhuman, godlike: mensae,: sententia,.— Hence, adv. in two forms.
ĭnhūmānē, inhumanly, savagely, cruelly: nimis graviter cruciat adulescentulum, nimisque inhumane,: facere contraque naturae legem,: muta (oratio),.— Comp.: inhumanius dicere,.—
ĭn-hūmānĭter, uncivilly, discourteously: me miratum esse istum tam inhumaniter fecisse, ut, etc.,; , acc. to P. (where the MSS. have inhumane).

la:verb:inhibeo.gloss: to lay hold of, keep back, restrain, curb, check, stop
senses: to lay hold of, keep back, restrain, curb, check, stop
la:verb:inhibeo.html:
ĭn-hĭbĕo, ŭi, ĭtum, 2, v. a.
in-habeo
,
to lay hold of a thing, in order to keep it back or to put it forward.
To keep back, restrain, curb, check.
Lit.: tela,; : crudelissimas manus,: frenos,: equos,: cruorem,: alvum,: remos,to cease rowing,: inhibere, or inhibere remis, or inhibere remis puppim, or inhibere retro navem, to row the ship backwards without turning it round; cf.: inhibere est verbum totum nauticum: sed arbitrabar sustineri remos, cum inhibere essent jussi remiges. Id non esse ejusmodi, didici heri ... non enim sustinent, sed alio modo remigant: id ab ἐποχῇ remotissimum est, . (Cicero himself has used the term in the incorrect signif. here found fault with: Ut concitato navigio, cum remiges inhibuerunt, retinet tamen ipsa navis motum et cursum suum, intermisso impetu pulsuque remorum,.) In the foll. passages it is used in its proper acceptation: cum divellere se ab hoste cupientes inhiberent Rhodii,: ite cessim inhibete remis, et a bello discedite,: Tyrii inhibentes remis aegre evellere navem quae haerebat,: retro navem inhibere,: postquam inhibent remis puppes,.—
Transf., to restrain, hinder, prevent, inhibit: impetum victoris,: facinus,: urentis oculos, blasting or evil eyes, .—
Ab aliqua re: a turpi mente inhibere probro,.—
With quominus: nec tamen potuit inhibere (Cato), quominus Romae quoque ponerentur (statuae),.—
With inf.: inhibentur rectum agere cursum,: inhibenda tamen est (mater mori),; . —
Sometimes in the sense of adhibere, exercere, to set in operation, to practise, perform, use, employ: hocine hic pacto potest inhibere imperium magister,exert authority,: utrum fontine an Libero imperium te inhibere mavis?: imperium in deditos,: imperium si quis inhiberet,: neque animis ad imperium inhibendum imminutis,: eadem supplicia alicui,to inflict the same punishment on one,; cf. coërcitionem,to inflict,.

la:noun:inhibitio.html:
ĭnhĭbĭtĭo, ōnis, f.
inhibeo
,
a restraining: remigum, a rowing backwards: inhibitio autem remigum motum habet, et vehementiorem quidem remigationis navem convertentis ad puppim,; v. inhibeo, I. A.

ĭnhŭmātus, a, um, adj.

la:verb:inhorreo.gloss: to bristle up; one's hair stands on end
senses: to bristle up; one's hair stands on end
la:verb:inhorreo.html:
ĭn-horrĕo, ŭi, 2, v. n.,
to stand on end,

stand erect, bristle.

Lit.: haud secus quam vallo saepta inhorreret acies,: spicea jam campis cum messis inhorruit,: aper pilis inhorrentibus corio squalidus,bristling,.—
Transf.
To have a tremulous motion, to quiver, shake, shudder: pennis agitatus inhorruit aër. : inhorruit aether, Luctificum clangente tuba,: inhorruit unda tenebris,.—
To cause to bristle up: aper inhorruit armos,.—
To tremble, shake, shudder, with cold, fear, horror: cum primum aliquis inhorruit et ex horrore incaluit,: inhorrui frigore,: in severitatem alicujus, ap. (Rep. 4, 6 B. and K.): domus principis inhorruit,: (Mercurius) tenui exceptus inhorruit aurā,.

la:verb:inhorresco.gloss: to begin to bristle (up); one's hair starts to stand on end
senses: to begin to bristle (up); one's hair starts to stand on end
to start to quiver, tremble or shudder (at)
la:verb:inhorresco.html:
ĭn-horresco, 3,
v. inch. n., to send forth sharp points, to rise erect, to bristle up.
Lit.: gallinae inhorrescunt edito ovo excutiuntque sese,: inhorrescit mare, Pac. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 411 Rib.): mobilibus veris inhorruit Adventus foliis (poet. for folia inhorrescunt, varie agitantur auris vernis), , v. Orell. ad h. l.: frigorum impatientia papiliones villis inhorrescunt,: trifolium inhorrescere et folia contra tempestatem subrigere,: Atlas nemoribus inhorrescit,.—
Transf., to tremble, shake, shiver.
With fever, : frigida potio inutilis est iis qui facile inhorrescunt,.—With cold: aër nivibus et glacie inhorrescit,: cum tristis hiems aquilonis inhorruit alis,.—
To quake, shudder, with fear, horror, : solitudo inhorrescit vacuis,. 85; .—Rarely with acc.: adeo rebus accommodanda compositio, ut asperis asperos etiam numeros adhiberi oporteat, et cum dicente aeque audientem inhorrescere,.— Transf., to shudder at: severitatis vim,.

la:adj:inhospitus.html:

Subst.: ĭnhospĭta, ōrum, n.plur., inhospitable regions: tanta inter inhospita,: per inhospita ducere vitam,.

la:verb:inhio.gloss: to gape, such as in amazement
senses: to gape, such as in amazement
to gaze with eagerness; to regard with longing
la:verb:inhio.html:
ĭn-hĭo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
, to stand open, to gape.
In gen.
Lit.: ora inhiasse luporum,.—
Trop., to gape with amazement, etc.: inhians Cerberus,: attonitis inhians animis,.—
In partic., to open the mouth wide, to gape at.
Lit.: Romulus lactens, uberibus lupinis inhians,: gazis inhians,: praedae,: pecudumque reclusis Pectoribus inhians, spirantia consu, lit exta, .—With acc.: postes,to gape at,.—
Transf., to gaze at with eagerness, regard with longing (cf.: capto, appeto, sitio): congestis saccis,: inhians in te, dea,; ; ; ; ; : lucro,: omnia, quibus vulgus inhiat,; , ext. 1: dictis,to hear eagerly, attend closely to,; .—With acc. (poet. and rare, except in Plaut.): hereditatem alicujus,: aurum,: mortem alicujus, Caecil. ap. ; : bona mea,: inhiat quod nusquam est miser,.
la:verb:inhio.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.

la:adj:inhonestus.html:
ĭn-hŏnestus, a, um, adj.
Dishonorable, disgraceful, shameful (class.): eho, impure, inhoneste, labes popli!: simus,: ignotā matre inhonestus,: vita,: exitus nobis non inhonestus,inglorious, (3, 22, 38 Müll.): mors, (2, 8 b, 27 M.); : vulnus,: (hostes) inhonesta vulnera tergo accipiunt,: pax,: Vitellius gulā et ventre sibi inhonestus, Orell. N. cr.: nihil injustum atque inhonestum, Auct. Or. pro Dom. 41: quid hoc joco inhonestius,more indecent,.— Sup.: inhonestissima cupiditas,: homo turpissimus atque inhonestissimus,.—
Unseemly, ugly, filthy: homo,; .— Hence, adv.: ĭn-hŏnestē, dishonorably, disgracefully: parere divitias,: accusare,: submitti alicui,: (with improbe) facere aliquid,.—Comp., .

la:verb:inhaereo.gloss: to stick or inhere in; stick, cleave, hang or adhere to; hold on to
senses: to stick or inhere in; stick, cleave, hang or adhere to; hold on to
to cling or adhere to, engage deeply or closely in; to be closely connected with
la:verb:inhaereo.html:
ĭn-haerĕo, haesi, haesum, 2, v. n.,
to stick in, to stick, hang, or cleave to, to adhere to, inhere in.
Lit.
With abl.: sidera suis sedibus inhaerent,: animi, qui corporibus non inhaerent,: visceribus,: constantior quam nova collibus arbor,: occupati regni finibus,: prioribus vestigiis,i. e. continues in his former path,: cervice,.—
With ad and acc.: ad saxa inhaerentes,.—
With in and abl.: in visceribus,: in rei natura,.—
With dat.: conjux umeris abeuntis inhaerens,: pectoribus nostris,: tergo,. — (ε) Absol.: linguae,: inhaesuro similis (canis), as if about to hang on the hare, i. e. to fasten on her, : dextram amplexus inhaesit,. —
Trop., to cling to, adhere to, engage deeply or closely in; to be closely connected with, etc.; with in and abl.: inhaeret in mentibus quoddam augurium,is inherent in our minds,.—Absol.: opinatio inhaerens et penitus insita,.—With dat.: virtutes semper voluptatibus inhaerent,are always connected with,: vultibus illa tuis, tanquam praesentis inhaeret,she hangs upon your features, gazes at,: pectoribus tu nostris inhaeres,: oculis animisque,: paene stulta est inhaerentium oculis ingeniorum enumeratio,that are before the eyes, plainly to be seen,: illa meis oculis species abeuntis inhaeret,: excidere proxima, vetera inhaerere,: memoriae inhaerent fidelius quae, etc.,: scio memoriae tuae preces nostras inhaerere, Plin. et Traj. Ep. 12, 1: studiis, to apply one's self to, : studio operatus inhaesi,: semper alicui,to be always about one,: Lysippum statuae unius lineamentis inhaerentem, inopia exstinxit,constantly intent upon,: conpendendis rebus pertinaciter inhaerere,to be obstinately bent on,.—With acc.: pejores inhaesimus laqueos,.

la:noun:inhumanitas.html:
ĭnhūmānĭtas, ātis, f.
inhumanus
,
inhumanity.
Inhuman conduct, savageness, barbarity: crudelitas inhumanitasque,; . —
Want of good breeding.
Incivility, impoliteness: quod ego non superbia neque inhumanitate faciebam. ; .—
